props.title: The Man From Snowy River II

sections.content: The sequel to the beloved Australian western **The Man From Snowy River** (1982), this 1988 follow-up continues the rugged frontier romance while expanding the scope of its predecessor. Like **Return to Snowy River** in some markets, the film follows Tom Burlinson reprising his role as Jim Craig, returning to the high country after making his fortune. It taps into the same vein of distinctly Australian western imagery that influenced films like **Quigley Down Under** (1990) and **The Proposition** (2005), with sweeping Victorian highlands replacing the American frontier.

sections.content: Director Geoff Burrowes captures the same majestic mountain scenery that made the original so visually striking, though with a darker emotional core. The sequel deals more explicitly with class warfare and land rights, themes that would later emerge in Australian films like **Australia** (2008) and **Sweet Country** (2017). Sigrid Thornton returns as Jessica, now caught between her love for Jim and her family's expectations, creating dramatic tension that echoes similar conflicts in **Far and Away** (1992). SUBHEAD: Australian Western Identity

The film cements the "Australian western" as a distinct subgenre, one that trades cowboys for horsemen and cattle stations for sheep runs. Like **The Overlanders** (1946) and **We of the Never Never** (1982), it portrays the unique challenges of the Australian frontier, where European agricultural traditions clash with the realities of an unforgiving landscape. The high-stakes horse riding sequences, particularly Jim's descent down treacherous mountain slopes, set a standard for practical stunt work that influenced later Australian action films.
